- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 74.23 → 75.48 or 73.50 → 75.70), then undercorrects.
- Underestimates in late forecast periods (last 5–10 days of 30d), suggesting mean reversion bias or lagged adjustment.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than true outcomes, missing volatility or sudden drops.
- Model exhibits persistent upward bias in the first 10–15 days, then gradually corrects — implies lagged response to recent history.
- Avoid extrapolating recent high prices into future; true outcomes often show downward correction after peaks.
- When history includes a recent spike, forecast should not overreact — cap overshoot at +5–10% above recent peak.
- True outcomes often dip below forecast mid-period — model may be overfitting recent trends.
- Use rolling 7-day mean of history as a baseline to adjust forecast if deviation exceeds ±3% from baseline.
